title: What if we harnessed Ball Lightning?
blob: what if we harnessed ball lightning? what if mysterious, glowing spheres, often mistaken for ghosts, held the key to limitless clean energy? ball lightning: a rare, luminous sphere, from pea-sized to meters wide, lasting over a minute. first recorded in 1195 by gervase of canterbury: a fiery globe near london. in 1638, an 8-foot ball of fire reportedly destroyed parts of a church in widecombe. even with 2014 video evidence, scientific data is scarce; lab effects are only visually similar. imagine capturing this intense, long-lasting energy. a single ball could power homes or even cities. harnessing ball lightning could transform our energy landscape. what other mysteries await discovery?

title: The Mariana Trench Mystery
blob: the mariana trench mystery 10,935 meters down, the pressure is 1,086 bar. that is 8 tons of weight on every square inch of your body. yet, at 10.6 kilometers deep, we found life thriving. these single-celled monothalamea survive 1,071 times sea-level pressure. the water is a freezing 1 to 4 degrees celsius. they live on crust that is 170 million years old. only 22 people have ever reached these crushing depths. the trench spans 2,550 kilometers, and it is mostly a mystery. what else is hiding in the dark? follow for more.
